- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1.5x prior peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment turns positive after a dip, model often fails to capture the rebound; add a small upward bias (e.g., +1–2% of recent range) to forecast.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >1.2x recent 7-day high, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (e.g., bearish sentiment), model tends to underestimate; add 2–3% buffer to forecast.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid extreme outliers (>±15% from 14-day moving average) unless sentiment strongly supports; use sentiment-weighted smoothing.
